profile.a: A five-person team for the Cambridge Finance Concentration Project, with backgrounds in non-profit, audit, corporate finance, data science and fintech.
Institutional investors such as pension funds and endowments deciding their allocation.
Should institutional investors increase their allocation to private credit?
Presented on 16 June 2025, using market data from 2000 to Q1 2025.
Mainly North America, with regulatory examples from the EU and Australia.
Private credit has grown about fourfold to $1.8tn since 2015, yet it is only 0.9% of institutional portfolios against 19.6% for all alternatives, and investors are divided on it.
Two interviews, three events, secondary research, an 11-risk register in three tiers, two pension-fund case studies, a recommendation and a six-criterion decision dashboard.

charts.title: How much of institutional portfolios goes to private credit (%)
charts.takeaway: Private credit is a sliver of the alternatives bucket, so the real choice is whether to take money from private equity and others, not whether to add a new asset class.

charts.title: The case for: private credit against its rivals
charts.takeaway: Lower losses than high-yield bonds and shorter funds than private equity. The team's own risk table warns that opaque valuations may understate the losses.

charts.title: The exit squeeze on private equity: US IPO value ($bn)
charts.takeaway: IPO value fell by about two-thirds in a decade. Credit, which is repaid rather than sold, gives a clearer way out than equity.

charts.title: Systemic risk then and now: large US banks' exposure (% of equity)
charts.takeaway: Banks are far less exposed to private credit than they were to mortgages before 2008, supporting the IMF view that stability risks are contained for now.

charts.title: Risk register: eleven risks in three tiers
charts.takeaway: The high-tier risks are the ones a typical pension fund is least able to absorb (illiquidity, defaults, recession, opaque valuation), which drives the 'most should not increase' verdict.

charts.title: Two pension funds, two approaches (%)
charts.takeaway: Very different allocations earn almost identical 10-year returns. What separates them is liquidity and governance: Arizona's predictable cash flows let it hold five times the share.

charts.title: Decision dashboard: return scenarios (%)
charts.takeaway: Even the pessimistic case is positive; the decision turns on whether an investor can bear illiquidity, not on the expected return.
